```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r install-ggplot2, eval=FALSE}
# Install ggplot2 (run once if it is not installed)
install.packages("ggplot2")
```

```{r load}
# Load ggplot2 and the built-in datasets used below
library(ggplot2)
data("mtcars")      # cars: mpg, weight (wt), cylinders (cyl), ...
data("iris")        # flowers: sepal / petal sizes for 3 species
data("economics")   # US economy over time (comes with ggplot2)

# Make cylinders a category so it can be used for colours and groups
mtcars$cyl <- factor(mtcars$cyl)
```

```{r geom-bar}
# 1. geom_bar(): bar chart that counts how many cars have 4, 6 or 8 cylinders
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Number of cars by cylinders", x = "Cylinders", y = "Count")
```

```{r geom-boxplot}
# 2. geom_boxplot(): compare the spread of mpg for each cylinder group
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, fill = cyl)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Miles per gallon by cylinders", x = "Cylinders", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-density}
# 3. geom_density(): smooth curve of how petal length is distributed per species
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Density of petal length", x = "Petal length")
```

```{r geom-histogram}
# 4. geom_histogram(): count of cars in each mpg range
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "orange", colour = "black") +
  labs(title = "Histogram of MPG", x = "MPG", y = "Count")
```

```{r geom-hline}
# 5. geom_hline(): horizontal line showing the average mpg
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(mtcars$mpg), colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Red line = average MPG", x = "Weight", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-jitter}
# 6. geom_jitter(): points moved a little so overlapping points can be seen
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = cyl, y = mpg, colour = cyl)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 2) +
  labs(title = "MPG by cylinders (jittered points)", x = "Cylinders", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-line}
# 7. geom_line(): line chart of unemployment over time
ggplot(economics, aes(x = date, y = unemploy)) +
  geom_line(colour = "darkgreen") +
  labs(title = "US unemployment over time", x = "Year", y = "Unemployed (thousands)")
```

```{r geom-point}
# 8. geom_point(): scatter plot of car weight vs mpg
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = cyl)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG", x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-rug}
# 9. geom_rug(): small ticks on the axes showing where each value falls
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_rug() +
  labs(title = "Scatter plot with rug marks", x = "Weight", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-smooth}
# 10. geom_smooth(): add a fitted straight line (linear model) to the points
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Weight vs MPG with a linear trend", x = "Weight", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-text}
# 11. geom_text(): write each car's name next to its point
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(mtcars))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(size = 2.5, vjust = -0.6) +
  labs(title = "Car names on the scatter plot", x = "Weight", y = "MPG")
```

```{r geom-violin}
# 12. geom_violin(): like a boxplot, but shows the shape of the distribution
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(title = "Sepal length by species", x = "Species", y = "Sepal length")
```

```{r geom-vline}
# 13. geom_vline(): vertical line showing the average mpg on a histogram
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "grey", colour = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(mtcars$mpg), colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Red line = average MPG", x = "MPG", y = "Count")
```
